title: Quieting noise sources and reservation reckoning after capacity surge
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Summary: A capacity surge on 2026-02-26 exposed a recurring noisy-tenant pattern that amplified reservation mis-sizing and an overly-permissive burst policy. The immediate result was elevated eviction churn, KV cache pressure, and 95th/99th token-latency regressions for multiple enterprise tenants. This ticket consolidates follow-ups, ownership, and a minimally disruptive rollout plan to (1) identify and quiet persistent noise sources, (2) reconcile reservation accounting with actual working set, and (3) tune burst policy to bound short-term spikes without harming latency for well-behaved tenants.
impact_analysis: Observed behavior: a small set (~3%) of tenants generated short high-QPS bursts that repeatedly evicted other tenants' KV caches and consumed ephemeral reservation credits. Reservation allocations were calculated off of a 95th-percentile window that underrepresented bursty tails for these tenants, causing insufficient soft-reserve hysteresis. The burst token bucket allowed immediate full-burst consumption without graceful decay, leading to oscillation. Telemetry: eviction_rate spike to 18/min (normal <2/min), KV cache miss ratio doubled for victim tenants, p95 token-latency increased by 2.4x and p99 by 3.1x for 4 hours. Root causes: noisy tenant workload patterns + reservation sizing heuristic mismatch + burst policy lacking decay/backoff.
goals: Reduce eviction churn to baseline (<=3/min) during similar bursts
Restore p95/p99 token-latency to within 10% of baseline for impacted tenants
Prevent single-tenant short bursts from causing cross-tenant KV-cache thrash
Provide observability + synthetic tests to detect regressions early
action_items: Signal-level triage: implement improved noisy-tenant fingerprinting (owner: Maya) — prototype in staging by 2026-03-06
Reservation reckoning: adjust sizing algorithm to use a blended 90/99 window and include working-set estimate (owner: Priya) — RFC + design review due 2026-03-08
Burst rework: add backoff-on-repeated-burst and cap instantaneous burst to X% of reservation with graceful token decay (owner: Diego) — PR and bench results by 2026-03-12
KV cache guardrails: implement eviction-rate circuit and tenant quarantine path that maintains degraded but stable latency (owner: Systems team) — implementation by 2026-03-14
Canary rollout: apply new policies to 2 dedicated clusters with synthetic noisy tenant for 72h before global rollout (owner: SRE) — plan by 2026-03-10
Synthetic tenants: add workload generator recipes that replicate observed short high-QPS patterns; integrate into CI cluster runs (owner: QA) — tests by 2026-03-11

Dashboards/alerts: add per-tenant KV miss/migrations, eviction_rate, burst_consumption_rate, and reservation_headroom with thresholds and runbook links (owner: Observability) — dashboards by 2026-03-09
Post-rollout retrospective: collect telemetry for one week post global rollout and run cost/latency analysis (owner: Sofia) — retrospective doc by 2026-03-28
acceptance_criteria: Eviction_rate <= 3/min during replayed noisy workload in staging
p95 token-latency <= baseline * 1.10 for victims in canary clusters
Burst policy prevents >50% immediate reservation consumption for repeated bursts
Automated synthetic test detects introduced noise pattern and fails CI when thresholds exceeded
Documentation and runbook updated with incident timeline and run procedures
updates: 2026-03-01 — Ticket created by Sofia. Triage meeting held; agreed to parallelize fingerprinting and reservation workstreams.

2026-03-03 — Maya: prototype fingerprinting algorithm (short-window spectrogram + signature hash) committed to feature branch. Early results show detection of recurring bursts with 94% precision in replay tests.
2026-03-05 — Priya: RFC posted for blended 90/99 reservation window; simulation on historical tenants suggests median allocation change +6% and 95th percentile reduction in eviction events.
2026-03-07 — Diego: burst cap implementation complete; bench harness shows bounded latency increase for capped tenants and reduced eviction ripple effect in the cluster simulator.
2026-03-09 — Observability: dashboards published; alert thresholds and escalation runbook linked. QA added synthetic noisy tenant test to nightly cluster run.
2026-03-10 — SRE: canary plan approved. Two dedicated clusters reserved (eu-west-1b, us-east-1c). Canary start scheduled for 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC.
2026-03-11 — Canary run started. Early telemetry indicates eviction_rate dropped 70% for impacted nodes and KV miss ratios stabilized. Monitoring in progress.
2026-03-12 — Decision: proceed with staged global rollout if canary maintains stability for 72h. Added follow-up to validate billing and cost impact post-rollout.
reviews_and_feedback: PM review (Jared Li): asked for clarity on customer impact and rollback criteria — updated dashboards with explicit rollback triggers
Design review (Emma Shah): recommended UX messaging for Console when tenant is quarantined; small copy changes merged
Security (Nikhil Rao): confirmed no change to data plane encryption; recommended audit log entries for burst-limit enforcement which were added
SRE (Amr Tayeb): requested an emergency kill-switch for burst policy; implemented feature flag and manual disable runbook
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive caps could throttle legitimate short-lived high-throughput customers. Mitigation: staged canary with traffic mirroring and opt-in tenant bypass for known high-throughput customers
Risk: Reservation sizing increase could raise unit costs. Mitigation: run cost model and include Optimize recommendations to offset with batching/quantization suggestions
Risk: Detection false positives may quarantine benign tenants. Mitigation: conservative fingerprinting thresholds and human-in-loop review for first 24h of any quarantine action
next_steps: Complete 72h canary and collect complete telemetry (owner: SRE)
Merge reservation sizing change after addressal of edge-cases found in simulation (owner: Priya)
Prepare rollout announcement and customer comms plan for enterprise SOC/CA (owner: PM)
Schedule post-rollout retrospective and bug triage session
